title: Streaming Hits Hollywood Hard: Here's Why with Producer Peter Hoffman
summary: Eisman argues that streaming maturity and migration from legacy margins weaken entertainment investments, especially Disney and debt-heavy Paramount. Hoffman describes presale financing, production risk and changing independent-film economics, using his own films as examples. Netflix reported the cited EPS slowdown, but its next quarter rebounded sharply. Disney historical margins support a difficult transition without proving permanent stock stagnation. Hoffman prosecution narrative is kept separate from Eisman views and checked against court opinions that preserve the convictions while acknowledging disputes over actual and intended loss.
assessment: The quarterly earnings comparison is accurate, but extrapolating it into permanent streaming weakness requires more evidence. Historical margin differences are real but heterogeneous. Private production anecdotes and legal accusations remain distinct from established financial or judicial facts.
speaker_map_notes: SPEAKER_01 is Eisman solo introduction; SPEAKER_02 is Eisman in the interview. SPEAKER_00 is Peter Hoffman. Brief interviewer questions embedded in SPEAKER_00 runs are inferred from dialogue and not treated as guest endorsements.
framework_points: Separate film quality, theatrical receipts and producer profit.
Presale contracts can transfer demand risk and support financing.
Financial capacity determines tolerance for creative overruns.
Past talent success reduces uncertainty only probabilistically.
Separate current quarterly growth from durable maturity.
Distinguish actual loss, intended loss and elements of fraud.
tools_and_charts: Disney and AMC historical stock charts
Film production budgets and territorial presales
State film tax-credit spending and court outcomes
transcript_cautions: Opening 60-230 seconds contains original substantive Eisman investment commentary, not a repeated montage.
Technical difficulties are disclosed and several phrases disappear around 580-612, 627-664, 964-980, 1107-1126 and 2007-2021.
Speaker labels split Eisman across two IDs and sometimes merge questions into guest answers.
Rambo 2 and Terminator 2 writing credits are conflated around 1410-1460; omitted as incidental film trivia.
Basic Instinct worldwide rank and stock-price comparisons require independent verification.
Hoffman is discussing his own contested prosecution; interviewing him does not make Eisman endorse his legal allegations.
